public_rationale: Sherlund Partners measured October 9–23, 2026 declines of 18.2% in its Datacenter Enablers basket and 11.9% in Silicon & Semis, supporting the valuation component [e1]. Gallup measured declining GenAI enthusiasm among US 14- to 29-year-olds in February 24–March 4 fieldwork, but that earlier survey does not establish declining enthusiasm during the October downturn [e2]. Navigator's October 1–5 survey reported 56% weekly AI use among registered voters, before the selloff [e3]. These items establish neither both conditions during a qualifying downturn nor continued practical AI and LLM use through that episode [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The market and sentiment measurements cover different populations and periods [e1, e2].
Concerns about financing the AI buildout do not independently establish declining enthusiasm for GenAI [e1].
The usage survey predates the October selloff and measures broad AI use, not subsequent LLM use for probabilistic prediction or generation [e3].

statement.excerpt: If enthusiasm for GenAI dwindles and market valuations plummet, AI won’t disappear, and LLMs won’t disappear; they will still have their place as tools for statistical approximation.
statement.document_title: CONFIRMED: LLMs have indeed reached a point of diminishing returns

from_speaker: If enthusiasm for GenAI dwindles and market valuations plummet
their place as tools for statistical approximation
our_interpretation: The condition requires both declining enthusiasm for generative AI and sharply falling relevant market valuations during an identifiable downturn.
The ordinary reading is that AI and LLMs retain practical uses through that downturn. It does not require widespread adoption, commercial growth, or reliable general intelligence.
I read statistical approximation as probabilistic prediction or generation used for practical tasks. The statement does not say this must be their only use.
The November post reaffirms the earlier quotation. I assess the reaffirmed forecast from November 9, 2024.
Neither an isolated stock decline nor continued use before the qualifying downturn establishes the conditional outcome.
criteria.support_condition: Both parts of the antecedent are independently established, followed by evidence that AI and LLMs retain practical uses through that downturn, including probabilistic prediction or generation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Both parts of the antecedent are independently established, followed by evidence that AI or LLMs have disappeared from practical use, or that LLMs no longer retain the stated practical role.

evidence.locator: Section “Two weeks, two different moves,” first paragraph
evidence.explanation: Its market baskets show a substantial October 9–23 selloff, including declines of 18.2% for datacenter enablers and 11.9% for silicon and semiconductors. This supports the valuation component, but the report describes financing concerns while saying inference demand remains strong; it does not establish both antecedents.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; survey dates in “Survey Methods”
evidence.explanation: The February 24–March 4 survey establishes waning enthusiasm among US respondents aged 14–29. Its population and timing do not establish a general decline in GenAI enthusiasm during the October market downturn.

evidence.excerpt: A majority (56%) of Americans report weekly AI use
evidence.locator: Section “A Majority of Americans Report Frequent AI Use and Primarily Use It For Research,” first paragraph
evidence.explanation: The registered-voter survey shows continued AI use and reports improved favorability since September. Fieldwork ended before the October 9–23 selloff, and broad AI usage does not directly measure LLM persistence after that episode.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated evidence establishing both declining GenAI enthusiasm in an identified population and sharply falling relevant valuations during the same downturn, followed by documented practical AI and LLM use through that episode, including probabilistic prediction or generation—or evidence that AI or LLMs disappeared from practical use or LLMs lost that role.
